environment: Owner Mac (macOS 25.6.0 arm64, node 26.8.2) against exclusively-owned PostgreSQL 16.15 databases on loopback. Production is untouched.

commands.action: Re-import with the same run id and the same source fingerprint
commands.command: node tools/v5-migration/cli.js load --model <private live model> --run e2e-run --database-url <owned target> --environment test --adopt-existing

commands.action: Import with a fresh run id into the same already-populated target
Interrupt a load mid-run and resume it
Prove the ledger hash is independent of the session timezone: same model imported into two databases whose server default timezone differs

assertions: The importer takes the same session advisory lock as the migration runner, so a second concurrent importer is refused rather than interleaved.
An unknown target is refused outright; a target whose schema is not migrated is refused before any write; a reopened target adopts its existing rows explicitly rather than implicitly.
A reused run id with a different source fingerprint or a different extractor release is refused, so a run can never be silently reinterpreted.

Batches are deterministic: the cursor is the last committed canonical key (never an offset) and the batch definition hash binds the projection definition, so a resumed run re-derives exactly the same row set.

A client aborted mid-batch leaves the already-committed batches committed and the interrupted batch re-executed on resume; the resumed batch records a non-null cursor and an increased attempt count, and the final target digest equals an uninterrupted run's.

Repeating the import under the same run id writes zero rows and verifies every previously committed row; a fresh run id converges, writing only the three singleton rows that are legitimately re-adopted with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.

No statement in the importer truncates or drops anything; a row collision with state the run did not write is a hard refusal, and a committed-row hash mismatch is a hard failure rather than an overwrite.

Row and primary-key hashes are computed in Node from an explicit column list using the shared canonicalizer, never from a server-rendered JSON form, so they do not depend on the session timezone: two databases with different server timezones produce byte-identical 5272-entry ledger digests.

No target row is generated by the import: actor, match, room, ticket, receipt and event identifiers all come from the source, and the reward-event identity sequence is advanced past the imported ids rather than left to collide.

not_claimed: G03 acceptance (the phase gate) or the Neon staging import
Production writes, production restore or cutover
sanitized_summary: Reruns and resume are safe: the import is serialized by the same advisory lock as the migrations, refuses an unknown target or a reinterpreted run, batches deterministically on the last committed canonical key, and resumes an interrupted run to the identical target. A repeated import is a verified no-op and a fresh run id converges. Hashes are timezone-independent: two databases with different server timezones produce byte-identical ledger digests.
review_notes: Only counts, hashes and structural facts are recorded; no actor id or raw row appears. The interruption, timezone comparison and fault injections were performed on owned disposable databases; production was never opened for write.
